entries.1.23: Likewise other accomplished ascetics, like the fire itself and righteous in conduct, gratified Rama the lord according to rule.
entries.3.27: He entered that vast wood, dark as a great cloud, furnished with great trees of many kinds, variegated with flocks of birds of every sort, filled with jackals and strewn with beasts of prey.
entries.4.2: "This is Rama, son of Dasaratha, truthful, of good conduct and pure; he is being carried off along with Lakshmana by a demon dreadful in appearance."
entries.4.33: Then, having slain the rakshasa and taken Maithili back, the two of them, he whose bow was bright with gold and his brother, roamed at will in the great wood, delighted, like the moon and the sun standing in the sky.
entries.9.34: "Out of a woman's fickleness I have urged this upon you; who am I to teach you dharma? Weigh it in your understanding along with your brother, and do without delay whatever pleases you."
entries.10.14: "We have the power, indeed, to kill the night-rangers by the strength of our penance; but we do not wish to exhaust the penance we have earned over so long a time."
entries.11.55: "— whose brother, of holy deeds, desiring the welfare of the people, subdued death by his penance and made this quarter a refuge."
entries.11.55.1: "Here once, so they say, dwelt the cruel Vatapi and Ilvala, two great asuras and brothers together, slayers of brahmins."
entries.11.94: "We have reached the hermitage, Saumitri. Go in ahead and announce to the sage that I have arrived here with Sita."
entries.14.29.1: "From the mouth the brahmins were born, from the breast the kshatriyas, from the thighs the vaishyas and from the feet the shudras: so says the sacred word."
entries.19.24.1: "Seeing those two brothers slain by you in battle, she will drink their blood in the fight, thrilled and delighted."
entries.25.43: Seeing them slain, all the rakshasas were utterly distressed and could not stir against Rama, conqueror of the cities of foes.
entries.43.34: "The lady of slender waist, Vaidehi, will sit with me upon the excellent golden skin of this gem among deer."
entries.45.41: Then Lakshmana, self-possessed, saluted Sita with joined palms, bowed slightly, and looking back again and again at Maithili, went to Rama's presence.
entries.46.13: Struck by the arrows of the god of love, that lord of the demons, chanting words from the Vedas, spoke humbly in that solitary place.
entries.64.72.1: The form of Rama, enraged and brought to such a state, the wise one, appeared as the form of Rudra appeared of old at the burning of the three cities.
entries.66.5: "If you will not bear this sorrow that has come, Kakutstha, what other man, ordinary and of little strength, shall bear it?"
entries.75.15.1: Then the splendid Rama, son of Dasaratha, having seen that lake Pampa along with Saumitri, lamented.
